items.kind: bug (impl selection, HIGH — blocks A112 S3)
items.title: SPECIFICITY — the impl-selection order does not rank a SUBTRAIT bound above its supertrait bound: `impl type S: Narrow<T>` vs `impl type S: Base<T>` where `trait Narrow<T> with Base<T>` → 'neither impl subject is more specific'. This is the optional-capability dispatch A112 S3 needs (`each` over a `DeltaSource` vs a plain `Source<List<T>>`), and both of the lane's spellings were refused
items.discussion: collections-39 (FIND 1; the S3 patch is WRITTEN and held at `sweeps/order39/collections-39/`); A112 (S3 lands unchanged once this and B379 are fixed — rec Q-B); B318 (the specificity order's home); B379 (the second gap)
items.body: Repro (with a control): `trait Base<T> { fun f(self) }`, `trait Narrow<T> with Base<T> { fun g(self) }`, `impl type S: Base<T> { fun h(self) }`, `impl type S: Narrow<T> { fun h(self) }` — a call `x.h()` on a type implementing both → 'neither impl subject is more specific'. `Narrow<T>` implies `Base<T>` by declaration, so `S: Narrow<T>` is strictly the smaller set and must win. Fix: the specificity comparison consults the trait inheritance graph (a subject bound by a subtrait is more specific than one bound by any of its supertraits). Pins: the repro selects `Narrow`'s; the reverse declaration order too; an unrelated pair still ties. Rec (collections' Q-B): rule B378 + B379 defects, fix both, land the held S3 patch unchanged; alternative an explicit `each_delta(..)` form — rejected as a second vocabulary.

items.title: a generic parameter reachable ONLY through a BLANKET impl's trait argument does not bind through a STRUCT-RETURNING constructor call: '`T` is missing the bound `: PartialEq`' — while the nominal-impl route binds, and a non-struct-returning call binds (with a control)
items.discussion: collections-39 (FIND 2); B378 (its sibling; both block A112 S3); B300 (closed — bound binders grounded from the receiver as a worklist; this is the CONSTRUCTOR-RETURN face of the same binding); B369 (closed — the caller's unsubstituted return type; check the seam)
items.body: Shape: `impl type S: DeltaSource<List<T>, SeqOp<T>> { fun rows(self): Rows<T> { Rows::new(..) } }` — `Rows::new` returns a struct generic in `T`; inside the blanket body `T` is known only via the bound's trait argument, and the constructor call reports `T` missing a bound the blanket's own where-clause carries. Replace the struct-returning call with a plain function returning `T` and it binds; write the impl nominally and it binds. Fix: the blanket body's binder environment must be the one `bind_subject_bound_binders` grounds, at CONSTRUCTOR calls too (the struct-literal/constructor path apparently re-derives from the nominal environment). Pins: the lane's repro + control; the held S3 patch compiles.

items.body: The index operator's receiver typing loses `K` when the receiver is a `read()` temporary (a `Shared<T>::read` answers `T` through the blanket; the subscript then asks the element type of an unresolved `T`), where the method call path resolves the same `T` first. items.title: `==` on a `T: PartialEq` LOSES its bound inside a nested `match` arm within a closure — the same comparison one level up type-checks
items.discussion: collections-39 (FIND 4, inside `reconcile`'s index; worked around by hoisting); B300 family; the closure-body binder environment (B372 is another closure-position loss this order)
items.body: Shape: `fun f<K: PartialEq>(..) { xs.each(|x| match x { Some(let k) => if k == key { .. }, None => .. }) }` → 'no operator `==` for `K`' (or the bound-missing form) inside the arm; `if k == key` written outside the `match`, or the `match` outside the closure, both check. Fix: the closure body's generic environment must carry the enclosing function's bounds into nested pattern-arm scopes (the arm scope appears to be built from the closure's OWN parameters only). Pins: the nested shape; two levels of nesting; a control outside the closure.
